rules.title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act rent limits, SB 567 version)
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered units may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local percentage change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, and no more than two increments in that period. The initial rent for a new tenancy is not capped, and rent-increase notices must follow Civ. Code § 827.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI change, max 10%, per 12 months; max two increases per 12 months

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property statewide (including mobilehome park tenancies), except exempt categories; sunset January 1, 2030.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes, condos) if owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management and proper written notice is given; owner-occupied duplexes (not ADUs/JADUs); mobilehome homeowners.
rules.interaction: yields to stricter local rule where the local rule covers the unit
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios de unidades cubiertas no pueden aumentar la renta más del 5% más el cambio porcentual del costo de vida local, o el 10%, lo que sea menor, en cualquier período de 12 meses, y no en más de dos incrementos en ese período. La renta inicial de un nuevo arrendamiento no tiene límite, y los avisos de aumento deben cumplir con el Código Civil § 827.
rules.caveat: Section was effective January 1, 2024 but operative April 1, 2024 by its own terms; it is repealed as of January 1, 2030. The percentage change in cost of living is recomputed yearly from regional CPI. | Secondary description on a city page; the maximum percentage is adjusted yearly and the page lists only 8.9% for Aug 2024–Jul 2025 and 8.8% for Aug 2023–Jul 2024, which are out of date as of the retrieval date. The page does not state the statute's effective date.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess rent, attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times the excess if willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious; enforceable by Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.effective_date_quote: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – statewide just-cause eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a covered unit continuously and lawfully for 12 months (or 24 months if an adult was added), the owner can end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance within 15 days or waive the final month's rent, and failure to comply voids the notice.
rules.key_value: 12 months occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation assistance for no-fault termination

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies after 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants added). Exempt: housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes; separately alienable property owned by natural persons (not REITs, corporations, or LLCs with a corporate member) with the required written exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotels, dormitories, certain care facilities. Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019 or a more protective later ordinance applies.

rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care and care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with owner; owner-occupied single-family (up to two units/bedrooms) and mobilehome owners; owner-occupied duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property with qualifying natural-person owner and notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.interaction: yields to stricter local rule where the local rule covers the unit
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: The document states the section becomes operative April 1, 2024, while the current amended text states it is effective January 1, 2026.
rules.requirement_es: Después de que un inquilino ha ocupado la unidad de forma continua y legal durante 12 meses (o 24 meses si se agregó un adulto), el propietario solo puede terminar el arrendamiento por una causa justificada, indicada en el aviso. En terminaciones sin culpa, el propietario debe pagar un mes de renta como asistencia de reubicación dentro de 15 días o perdonar la renta del último mes; el incumplimiento anula el aviso.
rules.caveat: Section sunsets and is repealed January 1, 2030 unless extended.
rules.penalty: Notice void; actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages (plus punitive damages) if willful or malicious; injunctive relief by AG, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 203, Sec. 1.   (AB 1529)   Effective January 1, 2026.   Repealed as of January 1, 2030, by its own provisions.)

rules.title: Relocation for temporary capital-improvement displacement under 20 days
rules.requirement: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement displacement of less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code § 1947.9 rather than SF Rent Ordinance § 37.9C; SF lists the current rate as $446/day plus actual moving expenses.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.requirement_es: Los pagos de reubicación por desplazamiento temporal de menos de 20 días por mejoras de capital se rigen por el Código Civil de California § 1947.9 y no por la Ordenanza de Rentas § 37.9C; San Francisco indica la tarifa actual de $446 por día más gastos de mudanza.
rules.caveat: Only a passing mention of the state statute on a city rates page; the daily rate is listed by SF for 3/1/26–2/28/27.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation benefits for lower-income tenants displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities pay under Gov. Code Chapter 16 (§ 7260 et seq.). Where higher, this State amount applies in addition to or in place of the City RSO/JCO amounts.

coverage_conditions.summary: Lower-income households displaced from Protected Units demolished for new construction.

rules.quoted_span: Pay relocation assistance to tenants in compliance with the State law’s Housing Crisis Act
rules.requirement_es: Los hogares de bajos ingresos (80% del AMI o menos) desplazados por la demolición de sus unidades para nueva construcción deben recibir beneficios de reubicación acordes con los que pagan las entidades públicas conforme al Cap. 16 del Código de Gobierno (§ 7260 y ss.). Cuando sea mayor, este monto estatal se aplica además o en lugar de los montos RSO/JCO de la Ciudad.
rules.caveat: Described only secondhand in a City of Los Angeles bulletin; the bulletin cites Gov. Code 66300.6(b)(4)(A) and says parties should seek legal advice on the state law.

rules.title: Security deposit cap: one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit (however named, including fees for processing a new tenant) of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Leases may not label any deposit "nonrefundable."

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Advance payment of six months' rent or more for leases of six months or longer; agreed tenant-requested alterations for a fee; two-month cap for small natural-person landlords (separate rule).
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede exigir ni recibir un depósito de garantía (con cualquier nombre) superior a un mes de renta, además de la renta del primer mes. Los contratos no pueden llamar a ningún depósito "no reembolsable".
rules.caveat: Secondary source: Berkeley Rent Board page explaining state law AB 12; statute section cite inferred. The Rent Board says it cannot determine whether a landlord can charge one or two months' rent.
rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention may lead to statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages (subd. (m)).
rules.effective_date_quote: This subdivision shall not apply to a security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.

rules.title: Deposit return and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out, the landlord must send an itemized statement of deductions and return any remaining deposit. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and necessary cleaning, and the landlord must provide photos and receipts for repairs.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Itemization/receipts not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning total $125 or less or tenant validly waived; initial inspection duties do not apply to certain unlawful detainer terminations.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:
rules.requirement_es: Dentro de 21 días calendario después de que el inquilino se mude, el arrendador debe enviar un estado de cuenta detallado y devolver el resto del depósito. Las deducciones se limitan a renta impaga, daños más allá del desgaste normal y limpieza necesaria, y debe proporcionar fotos y recibos.
rules.caveat: Effective date shown is that of the latest amendment (AB 414); the 21-day rule itself predates it. | Secondary source explaining state law; statute section cite inferred; different provisions have different start dates.
rules.penalty: Landlord acting in bad faith loses the right to claim any of the deposit; statutory damages up to twice the deposit (subd. (h)(7), (m)).
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

rules.title: Small-landlord security deposit cap: two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person (or an LLC of natural persons) and owns no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total may charge up to two months' rent as security. This higher cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlord is a natural person or LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent collectively.

rules.exemptions: Not applicable if the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador que sea persona física (o una LLC de personas físicas) y tenga no más de dos propiedades con un máximo de cuatro unidades en total puede cobrar hasta dos meses de renta como depósito. Este límite no se aplica si el inquilino es miembro del servicio militar.
rules.effective_date_quote: This subdivision shall not apply to a security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap and conditions
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and time, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjusted annually for CPI). No fee may be charged if no unit is or will soon be available, and the landlord must give an itemized receipt and return unused amounts.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners.

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador solo puede cobrar una tarifa de evaluación de solicitud hasta el costo real de bolsillo y el tiempo, y nunca más de $30 por solicitante (ajustada anualmente según el IPC). No puede cobrarla si no hay unidad disponible o pronto lo estará, debe dar un recibo detallado y devolver los montos no utilizados.
rules.caveat: The $30 cap is adjusted annually for CPI since January 1, 1998, so the current figure may be higher. | Secondary explanation on a city page; the cap is adjusted annually for inflation. | Secondary source (mirror of the statute). The $30 cap is adjusted annually for CPI, so the current dollar figure is higher. The document does not state the date the current text took effect.
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

rules.title: Screening fee refund and first-come process requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if they either consider complete applications in order received and approve the first qualified applicant, or refund the full fee to every applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days after the application, whichever is first.
rules.quoted_span: An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador solo puede cobrar la tarifa si considera las solicitudes completas en orden de recepción y aprueba al primer solicitante calificado, o si devuelve la tarifa completa a todo solicitante no seleccionado dentro de 7 días de elegir inquilino o 30 días de la solicitud, lo que ocurra primero.
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

rules.title: California Civil Rights Council criminal history screening regulations
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but may not use blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record or policies that consider arrests without convictions. The regulations also limit what criminal history can be sought and how it is used.
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source only — official text not captured; verify against the ordinance.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores pueden revisar antecedentes penales, pero no pueden aplicar prohibiciones generales a solicitantes con antecedentes ni políticas que consideren arrestos sin condena. Las regulaciones también limitan qué antecedentes se pueden pedir y cómo se usan.
rules.caveat: Secondary source (trade association); regulation section number not stated in the document and is inferred.
rules.effective_date_quote: In 2019, California’s Civil Rights Council (formerly the Fair Employment and Housing Council) enacted regulations that took effect Jan. 1, 2020

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination barred in rental housing
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot discriminate against or harass a renter or applicant because of their source of income, including Section 8 and other government housing subsidies or HUD-VASH vouchers. A landlord may still ask about the level or source of income.

coverage_conditions.summary: Owners of housing accommodations; no unit-count or building-age limits stated in this section.

rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede discriminar ni acosar a un inquilino o solicitante por su fuente de ingresos, incluidos los vales de la Sección 8, otros subsidios de vivienda del gobierno o los vales HUD-VASH. El arrendador sí puede preguntar sobre el nivel o la fuente de ingresos.
rules.caveat: Effective date is that of the 2023 amendment (SB 267); source-of-income protection may have been in the statute earlier. | Secondary agency summary (FEHA); statute citation is approximate and not given in the document. | Secondary source; statutory section inferred (SB 329 amended the FEHA 'source of income' definition).
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)

rules.title: Limits on criminal-history screening of rental applicants
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on applicants with a criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant and not a threat to safety or property.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most housing providers under FEHA, including third-party tenant screening companies.

rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, registros sellados o eliminados, ni registros de menores, y no pueden tener prohibiciones generales contra solicitantes con antecedentes penales. Negar una solicitud por una condena debe estar directamente relacionado con ser buen inquilino y no representar una amenaza para la seguridad o la propiedad.
rules.caveat: Secondary agency summary (FEHA); specific statute/regulation citation is not given in the document and is approximate.

rules.title: Subsidized-tenancy income standards and credit history alternatives
rules.requirement: Where a government rent subsidy applies, a landlord must assess income based only on the portion of rent the tenant pays. If the landlord uses credit history, the applicant may choose to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay, and the landlord must give reasonable time and reasonably consider it instead of credit history.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies in instances in which there is a government rent subsidy.

rules.exemptions: Landlord may still request information to verify employment, landlord references, or identity.
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.requirement_es: Cuando existe un subsidio de renta del gobierno, el arrendador debe evaluar los ingresos solo con base en la parte de la renta que paga el inquilino. Si usa el historial de crédito, el solicitante puede optar por presentar pruebas alternativas de su capacidad de pago, y el arrendador debe darle tiempo razonable y considerarlas en lugar del historial de crédito.
rules.caveat: Secondary source; effective date and exact statutory subdivision not stated in the document.
rules.effective_date_quote: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)

rules.title: AB 325: Common pricing algorithm ban (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software that uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices) as part of a conspiracy or combination to restrain trade. It is also unlawful to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to any person (not end consumers) using or distributing a common pricing algorithm for any product or service, including rental housing pricing software; not specific to housing.

rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal usar o distribuir un algoritmo de precios común (software que usa datos de competidores para recomendar o influir en precios) como parte de una conspiración o combinación para restringir el comercio. También es ilegal usarlo o distribuirlo si se coacciona a otra persona para que adopte el precio o término comercial recomendado.
rules.caveat: General antitrust provision that is not housing-specific; effective date computed under the constitutional default (chaptered Oct. 6, 2025, no urgency clause). Penalty details come from the digest and are not fully set out in the operative text. | Secondary source (law firm article); general cross-industry antitrust law that mentions apartment rental companies only as an example, not rental-specific.
rules.penalty: Violations of the Cartwright Act are punishable as a crime; the bill also lowers the pleading standard for antitrust complaints (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16756.1).
rules.effective_date_quote: 10/06/25 - Chaptered

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable and must follow municipal ordinances
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent only after properly ending the old lease and serving notice. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any local rent control ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act; no numeric statewide cap.

rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person
rules.requirement_es: El propietario solo puede aumentar el alquiler después de terminar correctamente el contrato anterior y dar aviso. El aumento no debe ser abusivo y debe cumplir con cualquier ordenanza local de control de alquileres.
rules.caveat: Unconscionability is fact-specific and judge-determined; no fixed cap. Secondary DCA summary.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover condominium/cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: If a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, the landlord may not raise rents to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents can still rise for new services or amenities.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to all tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, regardless of protected tenancy status.

rules.quoted_span:
rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion
rules.requirement_es: Si un edificio se convierte en condominio, cooperativa o propiedad en dominio absoluto, el propietario no puede aumentar el alquiler para cubrir costos derivados únicamente de la conversión. Sí puede aumentarlo por nuevos servicios o comodidades.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly built multiple dwellings are exempt from any municipal rent control ordinance for 30 years after construction is completed. Government-subsidized rents (HUD, NJHMFA) may also be exempt from local rent control.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to local rent control ordinances; newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt for 30 years after completion.

rules.exemptions: Units whose rents are subsidized by governmental funding, HUD-owned/subsidized developments, and NJHMFA-controlled projects are also not subject to municipal rent control.
rules.quoted_span:
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.requirement_es: Los edificios multifamiliares de nueva construcción están exentos de cualquier ordenanza municipal de control de alquileres durante 30 años después de terminada la construcción. Los alquileres subsidiados por el gobierno (HUD, NJHMFA) también pueden estar exentos.
rules.caveat: Secondary summary by DCA; statute enactment date not given.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to evict
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a statutory good cause to evict or refuse to renew a lease. Except for nonpayment of rent, the cause must be described in a written Notice to Quit, and the tenant need not move until a court enters a Judgment for Possession.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings and rooming/boarding houses.

rules.exemptions: May not apply to owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel/motel/guest house transient or seasonal guests (unless continual residence with no alternate residence); units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord must have 
good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53).
rules.requirement_es: El propietario debe tener una causa justificada legal para desalojar o no renovar un contrato. Salvo por falta de pago, la causa debe describirse en un Aviso de Desalojo escrito, y el inquilino no tiene que irse hasta que el tribunal dicte un fallo de posesión.
rules.caveat: Document is a secondary summary; the list of causes is in the next part of the document. | Secondary summary in a DCA Landlord-Tenant handbook; unit-count exemption described only indirectly.

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order, and only for specified causes such as holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, willful damage, or rule/lease violations. A three-day Notice to Quit applies to disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct, and a one- to three-month notice applies to lease non-renewal.

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings.

rules.quoted_span:
Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when 
a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.requirement_es: Los inquilinos de viviendas de dos y tres familias ocupadas por el dueño solo pueden ser desalojados por orden judicial y solo por causas específicas como permanencia tras el vencimiento, falta de pago, conducta desordenada, daño intencional o violaciones de reglas o del contrato. Se requiere aviso de tres días para conducta desordenada, destructiva o violaciones, y de uno a tres meses para la no renovación del contrato.
rules.caveat: Secondary summary in a DCA handbook.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to not renew a lease
rules.requirement: Most residential landlords cannot refuse to renew a written or oral lease unless they have a statutory good cause. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excepted.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental properties statewide, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels/hotels, transient or seasonal units.
rules.quoted_span: regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.requirement_es: La mayoría de los arrendadores residenciales no pueden negarse a renovar un contrato, escrito u oral, sin una causa justificada prevista por ley. Se exceptúan las viviendas de dos o tres familias ocupadas por el dueño, moteles/hoteles y unidades transitorias o de temporada.
rules.caveat: Only a passing mention in this part of the guide; the list of good causes appears in the Eviction section (later part). Citation given in source as 2A:18:61.3.

rules.title: NJ security deposit interest and holding requirements
rules.requirement: Interest or earnings on the security deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited to rent annually. The landlord must hold the deposit in trust in an insured NJ bank account and give the tenant written notice of the bank, amount, account type and interest rate within 30 days of receipt.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rentals; owner-occupied two-/three-family dwellings excepted unless tenant opts in; seasonal rentals (≤125 days) excluded from the account section.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-/three-family dwellings; seasonal rentals for the deposit-account section.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid
rules.requirement_es: Los intereses del depósito pertenecen al inquilino y deben pagarse en efectivo o acreditarse al alquiler cada año. El arrendador debe mantener el depósito en fideicomiso en un banco asegurado de NJ y notificar por escrito al inquilino el banco, el monto, el tipo de cuenta y la tasa de interés dentro de 30 días.
rules.caveat: Secondary summary guide.
rules.penalty: If notice/interest not provided, tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent after written notice and 30 days.

rules.title: NJ security deposit return within 30 days; double damages
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear or money owed. If the landlord fails to return it, the tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld plus costs and attorney's fees.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rentals including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings excepted unless tenant opts in.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (opt-in available).
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.requirement_es: Dentro de los 30 días posteriores al fin del contrato, el arrendador debe devolver el depósito más intereses, menos deducciones detalladas por daños que excedan el desgaste normal o dinero adeudado. Si no lo hace, el inquilino puede demandar por el doble de lo retenido indebidamente más costas y honorarios.
rules.caveat: Secondary summary guide.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees; $500–$2,000 civil penalty for willful withholding from tenants receiving government assistance.

rules.title: NJ security deposit cap (1.5 months' rent) and annual increase limit
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase cannot exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent held as security (including last month's rent) counts toward the cap.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rentals including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted unless the tenant requests in writing that the law apply (effective 30 days after request).

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in by written request).
rules.quoted_span:
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede cobrar un depósito de seguridad mayor a una vez y media el alquiler mensual, y cualquier aumento anual no puede exceder el 10% del depósito actual. El alquiler prepagado retenido como garantía (incluido el último mes) cuenta para el límite.
rules.caveat: Secondary summary guide (DCA Truth in Renting); not a statutory text.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge more than $50 as an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. Violators face penalties of up to $500 (first), $750 (second) and $1,000 (each later offense), and the overcharge is refunded to the applicant.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental properties statewide, except one- and two-family dwellings offered for rent and New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees (unless the licensee is the landlord).

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador o su agente no puede cobrar más de $50 por una solicitud o tarifa similar para alquilar o subarrendar una vivienda residencial. Las infracciones conllevan multas de hasta $500 (primera), $750 (segunda) y $1,000 (cada una posterior), y el cobro excesivo se devuelve al solicitante.
rules.caveat: The $50 limit is adjusted each January 1 by CPI change (only if positive), so the current cap may exceed $50. Effective date computed from approval on January 20, 2026.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, up to $750 second offense, up to $1,000 each subsequent offense; amount wrongfully charged remitted to applicant.
rules.effective_date_quote:
This act shall take effect on the first day of the
fourth month next following the date of enactment

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – disclosure before application fee and fee return
rules.requirement: Before taking an application fee, a landlord must tell you in writing whether criminal history is part of its screening and that you may submit evidence of inaccuracies or rehabilitation. If the landlord violates the Act, the Division on Civil Rights may order your application fee returned.

coverage_conditions.summary: Rental dwelling units other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span:
Prior to
accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to
the applicant:
rules.requirement_es: Antes de cobrar una tarifa de solicitud, el arrendador debe informarle por escrito si revisa antecedentes penales y que usted puede presentar pruebas de inexactitudes o rehabilitación. Si el arrendador viola la ley, la División de Derechos Civiles puede ordenar la devolución de la tarifa.
rules.caveat: Act sets no fee cap; it only addresses disclosure and refund as a remedy.
rules.penalty: Director may require that the applicant's rental application fee be returned.
rules.effective_date_quote:
This act shall take effect on the first day of the
seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source-of-lawful-income protection in housing
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to you because of the source of your lawful income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 HUD voucher.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, residential or business, except listed exemptions.

rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms by the owner or occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference for same religion.
rules.quoted_span:
a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede negarse a alquilarle por la fuente de sus ingresos legales o de su pago de renta, como un voucher de la Sección 8 de HUD.
rules.caveat: Secondary brochure (rev. 2015) that does not cite the specific LAD section; citation is approximate. Effective date not stated. | Secondary summary; quote is the tail of a sentence listing protected classes.
rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or to NJ Superior Court within two years.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – criminal history screening limits
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot ask about or consider your criminal record until after making you a conditional offer. After the offer, only certain recent or serious convictions may be considered, and the landlord may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment and written notice with reasons.
rules.key_value: Lookback after conditional offer: 6 years (1st-degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd-degree), 1 year (4th-degree); no lookback limit for murder, aggravated sexual assault, etc.

coverage_conditions.summary: Rental dwelling units offered for rent, other than units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units; landlord may still consider methamphetamine manufacture convictions in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede preguntar ni considerar sus antecedentes penales hasta después de hacerle una oferta condicional. Después, solo se pueden considerar ciertas condenas graves o recientes, y la oferta solo puede retirarse tras una evaluación individualizada y un aviso escrito con los motivos.
rules.caveat: Effective date computed from approval on June 18, 2021 plus 'first day of the seventh month next following'.
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (second within 5 years), $10,000 (two or more others within 7 years); possible return of application fee and up to $1,000 to applicant; enforced through the Division on Civil Rights, no court action.
rules.effective_date_quote:
This act shall take effect on the first day of the
seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic rent-pricing software or device that performs a coordinating function, and no one may perform a coordinating function or engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination of rents. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to any rental property owner (owning one or more residential rental units) and any coordinator; excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention facilities, and government affordability controls.

rules.exemptions: Research/statistical use not used to set rents, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, and government affordability controls are not a coordinating function.
rules.interaction: may preempt local ordinances once effective (flagged for review)
rules.conflict_note: May preempt local ordinances in the same category once effective; human review needed.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden pagar ni usar el software o dispositivo algorítmico de fijación de precios de un coordinador que realice una función de coordinación, y nadie puede realizar una función de coordinación ni participar en o facilitar la coordinación paralela de precios de alquiler. Las infracciones violan la Ley Antimonopolio de Nueva Jersey.
rules.caveat: Effective date computed from approval on July 20, 2026. Municipalities are barred from enacting conflicting ordinances. | Secondary source (law firm alert); summary of the law, not statutory text.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act; remedies under sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-6 through 9-17) remain applicable.
rules.effective_date_quote:
This act shall take effect on the first day of
the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.

rules.title: Statewide rent control ballot initiative (Initiative Petition 25-21) blocked by SJC
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide cap limiting annual rent increases to the lesser of CPI or 5% will not appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law and no statewide cap applies.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rental units; exemptions for owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.

rules.requirement: This bill would have let the city of Boston adopt rent stabilization, but it was not enacted: it was sent to a study order. No rent cap applies from this bill.

rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto habría autorizado a la ciudad de Boston a adoptar la estabilización de alquileres, pero no se aprobó: fue enviado a una orden de estudio. Este proyecto no establece ningún límite de alquiler.

rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease
rules.requirement: If you don't pay rent due under a written lease, your landlord can end the lease with a written 14-day notice to quit. You can stop the termination by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, on or before the day your answer is due in the eviction case. If the nonpayment was caused by a government delay in mailing or delivering a rent or subsistence payment, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if you pay in that time.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.

rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.requirement_es: Si no paga el alquiler adeudado bajo un contrato de arrendamiento escrito, el propietario puede terminar el contrato con un aviso escrito de desalojo de 14 días. Usted puede evitar la terminación pagando todo el alquiler adeudado, con intereses y costos, a más tardar el día en que vence su respuesta en el juicio de desalojo. Si el impago se debió a un retraso del gobierno en el envío o la entrega de un pago de alquiler o de subsistencia, el tribunal debe aplazar la audiencia al menos 7 días y tratar el arrendamiento como no terminado si usted paga en ese plazo.
rules.caveat: Applies to written leases only; effective date not stated in the document.

rules.title: Notice to terminate a tenancy at will (M.G.L. c. 186, § 12)
rules.requirement: A landlord or tenant must give written notice of three months (or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, the rental interval or 30 days, whichever is longer) to end a tenancy at will. For nonpayment of rent, the landlord may give 14 days' written notice to quit, and the tenant can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days if they have not received a similar notice in the prior 12 months.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days' notice to quit for nonpayment; 10-day right to cure

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies at will in Massachusetts.

rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.requirement_es: El propietario o el inquilino debe dar un aviso por escrito de tres meses (o, si el alquiler se paga con más frecuencia que cada tres meses, el intervalo de pago o 30 días, lo que sea mayor) para terminar un arrendamiento a voluntad. Por falta de pago, el propietario puede dar un aviso por escrito de 14 días, y el inquilino puede evitar la terminación pagando todo el alquiler adeudado dentro de los 10 días si no recibió un aviso similar en los 12 meses anteriores.
rules.caveat: This is a notice-to-terminate statute for tenancies at will; it does not itself require a stated 'just cause' for termination.
rules.penalty: If the required nonpayment notification is omitted, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in an action for possession.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must include state-developed form
rules.requirement: A landlord's written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must come with a form listing any repayment agreements, rental assistance programs, court rules and legal eviction restrictions, plus a statement that the notice is not an eviction and only a court order can force you to leave. Courts will not accept an eviction filing for nonpayment without proof the form was delivered.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to written notices to quit for nonpayment of rent given by a landlord to a residential tenant under c. 186.

rules.quoted_span: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to:
rules.requirement_es: El aviso escrito de desalojo (notice to quit) por falta de pago del alquiler debe ir acompañado de un formulario con los acuerdos de pago, programas de asistencia para el alquiler, reglas judiciales y restricciones legales sobre desalojos, y una declaración de que el aviso no es un desalojo y que solo una orden judicial puede obligarle a salir. Los tribunales no aceptarán una demanda de desalojo por falta de pago sin prueba de la entrega del formulario.
rules.caveat: Procedural notice requirement; the document does not state an effective date.
rules.penalty: Courts may not accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint in a nonpayment eviction without proof of delivery of the form.

rules.title: H.3744 – Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (sent to study order)
rules.requirement: This bill would have let Boston adopt tenant eviction protections, but it was not enacted: it was sent to a study order. No eviction rules arise from this bill.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto habría autorizado a Boston a adoptar protecciones contra el desalojo de inquilinos, pero no se aprobó: fue enviado a una orden de estudio. No surge ninguna regla de desalojo de este proyecto.
rules.caveat: Bill text not included in the document; specific eviction protections are not stated. Status inferred from the study-order action.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit cap and allowed upfront payments
rules.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord can charge no more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. The landlord must put the deposit in a separate bank account and give you a statement of condition.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential real property leases and tenancies in Massachusetts, other than short vacation rentals.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases or rentals of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.requirement_es: Al inicio del arrendamiento, el arrendador solo puede cobrar el primer mes de renta, el último mes de renta, un depósito de seguridad igual a un mes de renta y el costo de una llave y cerradura. El arrendador debe depositar el dinero en una cuenta bancaria separada y entregar una declaración del estado de la vivienda.
rules.penalty: Landlord who demands more than allowed or fails to comply with deposit handling forfeits the right to retain the deposit; treble damages for certain violations.

rules.title: Optional fee in lieu of security deposit (regulations authorized)
rules.requirement: The state housing office may issue regulations letting a landlord and tenant agree to an optional fee instead of a security deposit. The fee and any deposit together cannot exceed one month's rent, and the tenant can always choose to pay a full deposit instead.
rules.key_value: fee plus deposit capped at 1 month's rent

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies; optional for both tenant and lessor.

rules.quoted_span: the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit
rules.requirement_es: La oficina estatal de vivienda puede emitir reglamentos que permitan al arrendador y al inquilino acordar una tarifa opcional en lugar del depósito de seguridad. La tarifa y el depósito juntos no pueden superar un mes de renta, y el inquilino siempre puede elegir pagar el depósito completo.
rules.caveat: The statute only authorizes regulations; the document does not show whether such regulations have been issued.

rules.title: Security deposit held in separate interest-bearing account; annual 5% interest
rules.requirement: A landlord must hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account and give the tenant a receipt with the bank details within 30 days. If held a year or longer, the landlord must pay 5% interest per year (or the lesser amount the bank paid) to the tenant each year.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential real property leases and tenancies in Massachusetts.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases or rentals of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador debe mantener el depósito en una cuenta bancaria separada que genere intereses en Massachusetts y dar al inquilino un recibo con los datos del banco dentro de 30 días. Si lo conserva un año o más, debe pagar 5% de interés anual (o el menor monto pagado por el banco) al inquilino cada año.
rules.penalty: Failure to deposit in a proper account entitles the tenant to immediate return of the deposit.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days; permitted deductions; treble damages
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit within 30 days after the tenancy ends, and may deduct only unpaid rent or water charges, certain unpaid tax increases, and reasonable repair of damage beyond normal wear and tear. Any damage deduction needs a sworn, itemized list with estimates or receipts within the same 30 days.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential real property leases and tenancies in Massachusetts.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases or rentals of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador debe devolver el depósito dentro de los 30 días posteriores al fin del arrendamiento y solo puede deducir renta o cargos de agua impagos, ciertos aumentos de impuestos impagos y reparaciones razonables por daños (sin contar el desgaste normal). Para deducir daños debe entregar, dentro de los mismos 30 días, una lista detallada y jurada con presupuestos o recibos.
rules.penalty: Landlord forfeits right to retain any of the deposit; tenant awarded three times the deposit plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees (subsections 6 and 7).

rules.title: Licensed brokers may charge tenants fees with written disclosure
rules.requirement: Only a licensed broker may charge a prospective tenant a fee, and the broker must tell the applicant in writing the fee amount, how and when it is paid, and whether it depends on a lease being signed. The applicant signs the notice at the first personal meeting.
rules.key_value: Written broker fee disclosure signed by applicant

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to licensed brokers or salespersons; a landlord acting as his or her own broker is doubtful unless a separate bona fide business operation.

rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source only — official text not captured; verify against the ordinance.
rules.requirement_es: Solo un corredor con licencia puede cobrar una tarifa a un posible inquilino, y debe informar por escrito el monto, la forma y el momento del pago, y si depende de que se firme un contrato. El solicitante firma el aviso en la primera reunión personal.
rules.caveat: Secondary source; regulation cited generally as 254 C.M.R. 7 without section. Landlord-broker dual role is unresolved by appellate courts.

rules.title: Broker fees paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may work for either the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any fee must be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired the broker under a contract.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to fees for finding rental dwelling accommodations through licensed brokers or salespersons.

rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.
rules.requirement_es: Un corredor o vendedor con licencia solo puede contratar con el inquilino o con el arrendador, no con ambos. Cualquier honorario debe pagarlo únicamente la parte (arrendador o inquilino) que contrató originalmente al corredor mediante contrato.

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges by landlord or agent at start of tenancy
rules.requirement: Before or at the start of a tenancy, neither a landlord nor the landlord's agent can require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a one-month security deposit, and the cost of a key and lock.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases or rentals of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.requirement_es: Antes o al inicio del arrendamiento, ni el arrendador ni su agente pueden exigir al inquilino o futuro inquilino que pague nada más allá del primer mes, el último mes, un depósito de un mes y el costo de una llave y cerradura.

rules.title: Source-of-income / housing subsidy discrimination barred in rental accommodations
rules.requirement: A landlord or anyone offering rental accommodations cannot discriminate against you because you receive public assistance or a housing subsidy (such as rental assistance), or because of any requirement of that assistance program.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, without a stated unit-count or building-age limit in this subsection.

rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador o cualquier persona que ofrezca viviendas en alquiler no puede discriminarle porque usted reciba asistencia pública o un subsidio de vivienda (como asistencia para el alquiler), ni por los requisitos del programa de asistencia.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance – annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For rent-stabilized units, a landlord may raise rent only once every 12 months, by the allowable percentage set by the city. Since February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add a utilities percentage or a 10% increase for an added dependent; a 10% increase for an added non-dependent tenant is still allowed.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the allowable percentage

coverage_conditions.summary: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978 (plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28): apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family units on a parcel, hotel/rooming house rooms occupied over 30 days, ADUs/JADUs, mobile homes. Condominiums and townhomes: rent not regulated for tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995.

rules.exemptions: Rent may rise to market when the tenant voluntarily moves out or is evicted for non-payment or lease violation; Luxury Exemption available by application.
rules.quoted_span: Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under
rules.requirement_es: En unidades con estabilización de rentas, el propietario solo puede aumentar la renta una vez cada 12 meses, según el porcentaje permitido por la ciudad. rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance: relocation for demolition of Protected Units for new construction

rules.title: Cambridge policy order to ban algorithmic rent-pricing services (not yet law)
rules.requirement: The City Council passed a policy order starting the process to ban residential property managers from using companies' algorithmic or AI-driven models to recommend rents. It is not yet law; the city manager is to draft policy options or ordinance language for the Council later this term.
